ruleName: Relief Must Be Taken from Interference by No Play Zone
title: Ball in a No Play Zone (Practice Area)
question: Your tee shot comes to rest in a fenced-off practice area that the Committee has marked as a No Play Zone. What must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies.
You may choose to play it or take free relief.
You must take free relief. Playing the ball from the No Play Zone is not allowed.
You must take a one-stroke penalty drop.

explanation: A No Play Zone is an area on the course where play is prohibited, often marked by the Committee and sometimes fenced off. If your ball is in a No Play Zone, you must take free relief without penalty under Rule 16.1f; playing the ball from the No Play Zone is not allowed.

juniorVersion.title: Ball Stuck in a No Play Zone (Practice Area)
juniorVersion.question: Your ball lands in a fenced-off area on the course that has a sign saying 'No Play Zone.' What do you have to do?

choices.text: Hit the ball from where it is.
You can hit the ball or take a free drop, your choice.
You must take a free drop. Hitting from the No Play Zone is not allowed.
You must drop your ball and add one penalty stroke.

juniorVersion.explanation: A No Play Zone is a special spot on the course where you are not allowed to hit your ball. If your ball goes in there, you have to take a free drop outside that area. You can’t play your ball from a No Play Zone.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course, like behind a fence or a marked area, where you are not allowed to hit your ball.
You pick up your ball and drop it somewhere else (following the rules) without adding a penalty stroke.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids what a No Play Zone might look like on their own course. Use signs or ropes to help them learn where they can’t play from.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can choose to play from a No Play Zone.
Thinking you get a penalty for taking a drop from a No Play Zone.
